notes: Patient model reference (spec 09): hemorrhage classes, sedation and reversal behavior, complications the patient model must express, and the monitor channels. Doses live in drugs.json.

bloodLoss.note: Up to about 750 mL in a 70 kg adult.

signs.text: Heart rate normal or slightly raised; blood pressure unchanged
Heart rate 100-120, respiratory rate 20-24, narrowing pulse pressure
Marked hypotension, heart rate over 120, confusion, falling urine output
Pulse pressure under 25 mmHg, heart rate over 120, minimal urine output

hemorrhageModel.text: Bleeding rate follows the injury and falls as embolization takes effect; fluids, blood and REBOA move pressure.
hemorrhageModel.note: Model rule from the research notes; commercial simulators model trauma this way.

hemorrhageModel.text: A full bleed-out or cardiovascular crash ends the case; guided mode can pause first so the learner can work out the fix (questionnaire 1.15).

sedation.text: Oversedation shows as unresponsiveness, hypoventilation and apnea; the monitor shows falling saturation and rising end-tidal CO2.
sedation.note: Unresponsiveness, hypoventilation and apnea are from the protocol; the monitor signs are the model's expression of them.

sedation.text: After reversal, monitor 45-60 minutes, because sedatives can outlast the reversal agents.

contrastReactionPolicy.text: Contrast reactions are set by the case (allergy history) and never fire at random unless the case calls for it (questionnaire 2.9).

options: arterial pressure from the sheath side-arm
case labs: hemoglobin, platelets, INR, creatinine or eGFR, lactate
